title: Responsible for the Harm We Cause

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If people quarrel and one person hits another with a stone or with their fist and the victim does not die but is confined to bed, the one who struck the blow will not be held liable if the other can get up and walk around outside with a staff; however, the injured party must be compensated for the loss of their time and see that the victim is completely healed." - Exodus 21:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Quarrels happen. Tempers flare, and sometimes real harm is done. God's law does not pretend otherwise. What it insists on is responsibility. If you injure someone, you cannot simply walk away. You must make it right — cover their lost time and see them fully healed. Justice here is not about revenge but restoration.

There is deep wisdom for us in this. When we hurt someone — whether through our hands, our words, or our carelessness — the godly response is not excuses but repair. "I'm sorry" is a start, but love goes further and asks, "How can I make this right?" God cares about the person who was wronged, and He calls the wrongdoer to actively restore what was damaged.

This spirit of restoration runs all the way to the gospel. Zacchaeus, once he met Jesus, could not wait to repay those he had cheated, and Jesus called it salvation come to his house (Luke 19:8-9). Grace does not make us careless about the harm we cause; it makes us eager to mend it. A changed heart always looks for ways to heal what it has broken.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is there someone I have harmed whom I need to actively make things right with?
Do I take responsibility for my mistakes, or make excuses?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when I cause harm, keep me from excuses. Give me a heart that takes responsibility and works to restore, just as Your grace has restored me. Amen.
